topic: Linear Systems & Fundamental Subspaces: A Visual Journey

outline.topic: Linear Systems & Fundamental Subspaces: A Visual Journey

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation: The Intersection of Worlds
sections.content: Introduce linear systems as the intersection of lines/planes. Use a 2D coordinate system where two linear equations represent two lines. Emphasize that the solution is the point where they cross (or the line if they are identical).
sections.example: Visualizing two paths of 'Robot A' and 'Robot B'; where their paths cross is the unique solution coordinate (x, y).

sections.title: The Inverse Matrix: The 'Undo' Button
sections.content: Explain the inverse matrix as the transformation that reverses a linear operation. If matrix A maps a vector to a new position, A⁻¹ maps it back to the origin state. Prerequisite: Understanding matrix-vector multiplication as a transformation.
sections.example: A 'Spatial Teleporter' device: Matrix A moves a cat from Point A to Point B; the inverse matrix A⁻¹ acts as the 'Return Home' button to bring the cat back.

sections.title: Column Space: The Reach of a Transformation
sections.content: Define column space as the span of the column vectors. It represents all possible destinations (output space) reachable by the matrix transformation. Visualize this as a 'reachable region' on the 2D/3D plane.
sections.example: A 'Paint Brush' robot: The column space represents the total area on the canvas the robot can cover given its two mechanical arm vectors.

sections.title: Null Space: The 'Ghost' Zone
sections.content: Define null space as the set of vectors that the matrix collapses to the zero vector. Visualize this as the 'Kernel'—what gets 'deleted' or flattened by the transformation.
sections.example: A 'Magic Lens': Anything placed inside the null space zone of the lens becomes invisible (mapped to zero) when viewed through the lens.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Connect the concepts: If a matrix has an inverse, the column space spans the whole room and the null space contains only the origin point. Review the interplay between geometry and algebra.
sections.example: A 'Dimensional Map': A square matrix is like a complete map (invertible); a singular matrix is like a map folded flat into a line (losing information in the null space).

storyboard.title: Geometric Interpretation: The Intersection of Worlds
lecture_lines: Linear systems represent the intersection of lines.
Two equations define two distinct paths.
Their intersection point is the unique solution.
animations: Line 1: Fade in two 2D basis vectors, i-hat and j-hat.
Line 2: Apply a linear transformation matrix to grid space.
Line 3: Highlight the new positions of i-hat and j-hat.
Line 4: Draw grid lines distorting based on the matrix transformation.
Line 5: Visualize the determinant as the area of transformed grid.

storyboard.title: The Inverse Matrix: The 'Undo' Button
lecture_lines: Inverse matrices act as undo buttons.
Matrix A transforms a vector's position.
Inverse A brings the vector home.
animations: Line 1: Display an identity matrix and a transformed matrix.
Line 2: Show the inverse matrix as reversing the transformation.
Line 3: Animate a point returning to its original position.

storyboard.title: Column Space: The Reach of a Transformation
lecture_lines: Column space is the reach of transformation.
It spans all possible reachable destinations.
Visualize this as a reachable region.
animations: Line 1: Display column vectors of a matrix in 3D.
Line 2: Span the space covered by these column vectors.
Line 3: Indicate that all output vectors lie within this span.

storyboard.title: Null Space: The 'Ghost' Zone
lecture_lines: Null space collapses vectors to zero.
It acts as a ghost zone.
Everything here becomes invisible to transformation.
animations: Line 1: Identify vectors mapped to the zero vector.
Line 2: Highlight the line or plane forming the null space.
Line 3: Illustrate the null space as a sub-dimension.

storyboard.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: Invertible matrices span the whole space.
Singular matrices collapse dimensions into lines.
Algebra connects deeply with geometric intuition.
animations: Line 1: Display the linear transformation equation on screen.
Line 2: Summarize key concepts: determinant, inverse, and space.
Line 3: Final overview showing connections between these concepts.
